title: Coordinated sidecar-proxy drain + staged runtime rollforward for VPC upgrades
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement an orchestrated, health-gated drain and staged rollforward strategy for private (VPC) data-plane/runtime upgrades that leverages sidecar proxies and Terraform lifecycle hooks to achieve zero-downtime upgrades and automated safe rollback. The mechanism coordinates control-plane commands, sidecar drain signals, KV-cache prewarming, and traffic cutover with validation gates. Target environments: customer VPCs and private on-prem clusters where we cannot rely on cloud load balancer blue/green features.
comments: 2025-02-13: Spike complete. Verified sidecar drain signal via HTTP /_health/drain works with envoy-based sidecars in staging. Observed graceful connection termination but KV-cache eviction timing needs tuning.

2025-02-14: Design review notes - PM asked for explicit rollback observability hooks and a safety timeout. Decided to implement a two-stage rollback: immediate soft-fallback (route to previous runtime variant) plus an aggressive evict+rehome if errors persist > 3m.
2025-02-15: Engineering sync - agreed to implement Terraform null_resource hooks that call the orchestrator API for prewarm/commit/drain phases. Owner: infra-runtime team.

2025-02-17: PoC run in staging with synthetic traffic (QPS 200). Cutover completed with no 5xx spikes and P99 latency at 1.18x baseline. A cache-warm race found when concurrent prewarm and drain overlap; added a quorum-based prewarm confirmation.
2025-02-18: PR opened for orchestrator changes and sidecar drain endpoint: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2345. Requesting review from @Lena Kim and @Owen Park.
2025-02-19: Design feedback from security: require KMS session handoff log and mask any customer identifiers in upgrade telemetry. Added to scope.
2025-02-20: Staging run with terraform module hooks branch. Next: extend health probes to include model-serving readiness and add automated rollback policy in operator controller.
acceptance_criteria: No customer-facing 5xx errors attributable to the upgrade during staged rollouts
P99 latency remains within 1.3x of pre-upgrade baseline across staged tenants
Automated rollback triggers if error rate > 1% or if validation gate fails for two consecutive validation windows
Terraform apply + orchestrator sequence completes end-to-end in staging with explicit prewarm confirmation before cutover
Audit logs include KMS session handoff records and operator decisions for each stage
implementation_notes: Plan uses a five-phase orchestration: 1) Prevalidate (check node health, disk, KMS session), 2) Prewarm (spawn new runtime instances and run KV-cache priming jobs with quorum confirmation), 3) Drain (signal sidecar proxies via /_health/drain and pause new connections, wait for in-flight streams to finish or soft-timeout), 4) Cutover (update routing in the orchestrator and record metrics), 5) Validate (synthetic probes + customer traffic sampling). If validation fails, orchestrator routes traffic back to previous runtime variant and triggers a background aggressive rehome. Terraform integration: null_resource hooks call the orchestrator API with idempotent commands and expose a status resource for CI to gate the apply. Health checks additionally verify model-serving readiness endpoints and KV-cache integrity. Observability: emit stage markers to tracing, surface stage timelines in console rollout view, and include automated incident note templates for failed rollouts.
